summary:
Today's best opportunity is a Lane C story. The full retatrutide sleep apnea results (TRIUMPH-1-OSA and TRIUMPH-2-OSA) came out in NEJM on Oct 24. Medical Xpress and Physicians Weekly have covered it, but there are very few consumer explainers. That makes it a same-day long-form ("Retatrutide for Sleep Apnea: What the New Trials Found") plus a 20:00 funnel Short that names it. Caveat: the Sept 29 topline already got trade-press coverage, so the hook should be the NEJM paper itself.

Second is a strong retatrutide "what's confirmed?" Short. A Penn study in JAMA Network Open used AI to read about 149,000 Reddit posts from people who say they take gray-market retatrutide. The top unexpected report was more appetite, not less. The authors say this does not prove the drug caused it. Futurism's Oct 24 piece on bodega retatrutide keeps the story moving.

Third is a fit for the "What Is [new drug]?" hypothesis. Hanmi's efpeglenatide, Korea's first home-grown GLP-1 for obesity, launches there around Oct 29. In its Phase 3 trial of 448 people, weight fell 9.02% versus 0.89% on placebo at 40 weeks. It's a new name with almost no English explainers, so it's the closest thing to EloraTZP.

Evergreen Lane A topics are still accelerating: tirzepatide side effects (seen in 8 snapshots, now with new reviews on nausea and on pancreas and gallbladder events), stopping semaglutide or tirzepatide, and Thanksgiving eating, which starts climbing in early November. Good "honest uncertainty" body-worry tests: the pancreas and gallbladder review, the Wegovy versus Ozempic eye-stroke signal, and the bone systematic review published Oct 23.

Rejected: Yahoo's Oct 24 "GLP-1 microdosing" piece and the ongoing retatrutide "research-grade sourcing" and needle-free peptide vendor content.

Not verified yet: the HCPLive retatrutide kidney result could not be confirmed past the trial registry, and the PubMed abstracts for the depression RCT and the bone review didn't load. Pull the abstracts before writing scripts on any of these.

candidates.topic: Retatrutide for obstructive sleep apnea: full TRIUMPH-1-OSA (no diabetes) and TRIUMPH-2-OSA (type 2 diabetes) results published in NEJM, Oct 24, 2026
candidates.angle: Lane C, same-day 'New GLP-1 Drug Decoded'. Explain in plain terms what 'about 25 fewer breathing pauses an hour versus about 10 on placebo' means for sleep, who was studied (BMI 27 or higher, moderate-to-severe OSA, 80 weeks), and how it compares with tirzepatide's approved OSA use (indirect only). Give the dated status: investigational, not approved anywhere. Mention common stomach side effects. Title idea: 'Retatrutide for Sleep Apnea: What the New Trials Found' (52 characters).
keywords: new drug for sleep apnea weight loss
candidates.why_now: The NEJM paper came out today (Oct 24) and Medical Xpress and Physicians Weekly picked it up within hours. The Sept 29 topline was covered mostly by trade press. Retatrutide is our highest-peaking Shorts name (253, 196), and Lane C long-forms have a median of 47, our only proven long-form lane. The S1 10-24 Short was dropped for masking, so no published Short blocks a long-form.

evidence.signal: NEJM publication of both phase 3 OSA trials. Doses 4, 9 and 12 mg versus placebo over 80 weeks. The higher doses cut about 25 events an hour versus about 10 on placebo, and 39–52% reached no or mild OSA without excessive sleepiness versus about 13% on placebo.
Earlier topline: AHI fell by up to 36.1 events an hour (60.6%) from a baseline of 58.6.
TRIUMPH-1 basket trials for knee osteoarthritis and OSA. Shows the news was split across two cycles.

candidates.topic: What do people buying gray-market retatrutide actually report? Penn AI study of about 149,000 Reddit posts (JAMA Network Open, Oct 2026): increased appetite was the top unexpected report
candidates.angle: 'What's Actually Confirmed?' Short in honest-uncertainty style. Among 7,823 users with a classifiable symptom: fatigue 15.2%, nausea 11.6%, faster heart rate 4.8%. The authors say they can't tell whether retatrutide caused this or whether the vials even contained it. Contrast with what the controlled trials found. Point viewers to a prescriber about approved options or trials. Never name sellers. Pinned comment asks for saves only.
candidates.why_now: ScienceDaily (Oct 21–22), Epocrates and SciTechDaily covered it, and Futurism's 'bodega retatrutide' chemical-analysis story (Oct 24) keeps gray-market retatrutide in the news. Gray-market 'what's confirmed?' Shorts have a median of 103, and retatrutide Reddit got 120.

evidence.signal: Penn researchers analysed about 150,000 Reddit posts from about 40,000 users. Increased appetite was the most striking finding. The authors caution they can't attribute it to the drug.
Breakdown: 13,589 users reporting current use, 7,823 with a symptom. Fatigue 15.2%, nausea 11.6%, insomnia 6.1%, heart rate 4.8%.
'Someone Ran a Chemical Analysis of Bodega Retatrutide'. Mainstream follow-on coverage.

candidates.topic: What is efpeglenatide? Korea's first home-grown GLP-1 obesity drug (Hanmi) launches around Oct 29, 2026
candidates.angle: Pipeline explainer in the 'What Is [new drug]?' test. Cover how it works (long-acting GLP-1), the Phase 3 result (448 Korean adults, 9.02% versus 0.89% placebo at 40 weeks), and the trade-off reported in coverage: less weight loss than semaglutide or tirzepatide, with lower reported nausea and vomiting rates. Dated status: approved by Korea's MFDS only, not in the US, UK, Canada or Australia. No 'beat' frame.
candidates.why_now: Korea Biomedical Review (Oct 23) confirms an Oct 29 launch, so a dated news hook is coming. Almost no English-language YouTube explainers exist, which is the EloraTZP pattern (a new name with no competition).

evidence.signal: MFDS approval. 448 participants, 9.02% versus 0.89% weight loss at 40 weeks, with fewer GI side effects reported.
Hanmi's first Korean-developed GLP-1 obesity drug set for an Oct 29 launch.

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) side effects: which are common and what helps. New reviews on how nausea is measured in GLP-1 trials (Diabetes Obes Metab, Oct 22) and GLP-1 gut motility (Neurogastroenterol Motil, Oct 2026)
candidates.angle: Lane A search-question long-form. Use the trial rates of nausea, diarrhoea and constipation by dose (SURMOUNT-1), when they usually peak and ease, and evidence-based comfort habits (smaller meals, slower eating, fluids, fibre). Add The Conversation's point that nausea is under-measured in trials. Include the label's 'call your provider right away' wording for warning signs.
keywords: how long does tirzepatide nausea last
candidates.why_now: Seen in 8 snapshots with momentum holding at 74–78. A new DOM nausea review (Oct 22), The Conversation (Oct 22), Healthline real-patient experiences (Oct 23) and Drugwatch (Oct 22) give it a fresh hook. Tirzepatide-first titles are our proven Shorts lever.

evidence.signal: Narrative review of gaps in how nausea is measured in GLP-1 obesity trials.
GI symptom events and motility changes with GLP-1 RAs.
'GLP-1 drugs change how people eat, but nausea needs closer study'.

candidates.topic: Does tirzepatide affect the pancreas or gallbladder? New scoping review of pancreatic and gallbladder events with tirzepatide in obesity (Dove Medical Press, Oct 22, 2026)
candidates.angle: 'Honest uncertainty' body-worry Short ('What This Review Can't Say'). Say what the trials and review found, how rare the events are in absolute terms, and the symptoms the label says to call a provider about right away. Calm tone, no scare face, and the prescriber line.
candidates.why_now: The playbook asks for 2 more honest-uncertainty tests on pancreas and gallbladder after the macular degeneration Short (104 on YouTube, 160 on Instagram). The review is fresh, and body-worry topics do best on Instagram.

evidence.signal: Scoping review: pancreatic and gallbladder adverse events with tirzepatide in obesity management.

candidates.topic: Wegovy versus Ozempic and 'eye stroke' (NAION): why an FDA-report signal looked stronger for Wegovy, and what newer cohorts show (Medical Economics, Oct 23; Clin Ophthalmol, Oct 12; Cureus, Oct 19)
candidates.angle: Two-drug, honest-uncertainty Short. Explain disproportionality signals from adverse-event reports versus actual risk. Experts call the absolute risk very low, and the EU label now lists NAION. Give the sudden-vision-change 'call right away' advice. Name both products, with semaglutide first.
candidates.why_now: Medical Economics' Oct 23 roundup plus two October retrospective cohorts. The eye theme is our best-performing body-worry topic (macular degeneration 104 and 160).

evidence.signal: 'Wegovy may pose higher risk of eye stroke than other GLP-1 drugs'.
Single-centre cohort on semaglutide, diabetic retinopathy and NAION in type 2 diabetes.
GLP-1s may be linked to vision loss, but the overall risk is 'very, very low'.

candidates.topic: What happens when you stop semaglutide or tirzepatide? SURMOUNT-4 and STEP 1 extension regain, plus the new study of sustained versus minimal GLP-1 exposure in older adults without diabetes (Diabetes Obes Metab, Oct 22)
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form. Show the regain curves honestly, what helped people keep results in the trials (protein, strength training), and why any decision to stop belongs with a prescriber. No stopping or tapering instructions.
keywords: what happens when you stop tirzepatide
candidates.predicted_peak: steady; New Year spike in January
candidates.why_now: Seen in 8 snapshots. A new DOM older-adult exposure study (Oct 22) and the real-world persistence data (Oct 19) add fresh facts. It's one of the playbook's named Lane A titles.

evidence.signal: Sustained versus minimal GLP-1 RA exposure and metabolic outcomes in older adults without diabetes.
Real-world US semaglutide initiation behaviours, early discontinuation and 1-year persistence.

candidates.topic: Thanksgiving on tirzepatide or semaglutide: smaller plates, protein first, and easing fullness and nausea at holiday meals
candidates.angle: 'Life on GLP-1' Lane A long-form, posted in early November. Base it on how gastric emptying works and on dietitian and academic medical centre guidance (UC Davis Health). Encouraging tone, no restriction messaging. Short spin-off framed as an outcome question with tirzepatide named, never as a '3 ways' list.
candidates.why_now: Seen in 6 snapshots and seasonal searches start in early November. Publishing about 2 weeks ahead lets the video build search traffic before the peak.

evidence.source: Previous snapshot: UC Davis Health guide (Oct 20)
evidence.signal: Holiday meal guidance for GLP-1 users.
Obesity doctor on getting the best results with GLP-1s (eating habits).

candidates.topic: EloraTZP (eloralintide plus tirzepatide): Phase 3 starts in Q4 2026. New Drug Topics recap (Oct 24) of 23.3% versus 14.8% weight loss at 48 weeks in obesity with type 2 diabetes
candidates.angle: 20:00 funnel Short that sends viewers to our live EloraTZP long-form (499 views, our best). Add one new fact: Lilly's Q4 2026 Phase 3 start and what an amylin agonist adds. Population is obesity or overweight with type 2 diabetes. Phase 2b, investigational. Say 'top dose combination' and name both arms.
candidates.why_now: Drug Topics re-surfaced the result on Oct 24, and 'what is the new eli lilly drug for weight loss' queries keep appearing. It's our strongest long-form, so a funnel Short can push more viewers to it.

evidence.signal: Up to 23.3% weight loss and a 2.9% A1C drop over 48 weeks versus 14.8% on tirzepatide 15 mg.
Phase 3 to start Q4 2026.
'EloraTZP Shows Greater Weight Loss, A1C Reduction Than Tirzepatide'.

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide: how much of the weight lost is muscle? SURMOUNT-1 body-scan substudy, plus new muscle-sparing add-on trials (trevogrumab, bimagrumab with semaglutide)
candidates.angle: Outcome-question Short with tirzepatide first. Give the SURMOUNT-1 DXA lean versus fat split, then a 'what's coming' beat on investigational muscle-preserving antibodies. Say clearly that they're unapproved and that strength benefit isn't shown. Close on protein and resistance training as the supported steps today.
keywords: how much weight loss is muscle Zepbound
candidates.why_now: Earth.com (Oct 24) put muscle-preservation therapy back in the news. The muscle outcome-question format got 131 and 101. Seen in 7 earlier snapshots.

evidence.signal: Trevogrumab roughly halved semaglutide-associated lean mass loss at 26 weeks (6.6% versus 3.4–3.9%). Effect on function not established.
Meta-analysis of handgrip strength on semaglutide.

candidates.topic: Do GLP-1 medicines weaken bones? New systematic review of skeletal effects in adults with overweight or obesity (Arch Osteoporos, Oct 23, 2026)
candidates.angle: Honest-uncertainty Short. Say what bone density and fracture data show so far, why fast weight loss can affect bone, and the supported steps (protein, resistance and impact exercise, talking to a clinician about bone health). Pull the abstract before scripting.
candidates.why_now: The review was published yesterday and there's no mainstream pickup yet. It's a common worry among women 50+ in our audience and pairs with the muscle content.

evidence.signal: Systematic review of the skeletal effects of GLP-1 RA therapy in adults with overweight or obesity.

candidates.topic: Orforglipron (Foundayo) versus the Wegovy pill: what the new indirect comparison shows (Pharmafile, Oct 23), as oral semaglutide uptake nears injectable levels (AJMC and HealthDay, Oct 22–23)
candidates.angle: Head-to-head Short naming both pills, labelled 'indirect', with dated status for each, common side effects for each, and the 'don't switch on your own' line. Also usable as a Lane A long-form: 'GLP-1 Pills: Wegovy Pill vs Orforglipron, What's the Difference?'
candidates.why_now: There are many 'Wegovy pill' search-style queries in the feeds (pros and cons, how effective, when available) plus new uptake data. Orforglipron alone underperformed (36–39), so pair it with the Wegovy pill.

evidence.signal: Orforglipron shows weight and glucose advantages over oral semaglutide in an indirect comparison.
Oral semaglutide uptake near injectable levels within 3 months.

candidates.topic: Do 'GLP-1 boosters' and supplements work like semaglutide? Reuters/Japan Today (Oct 23) on doctors and regulators raising flags, and Fortune's 'best GLP-1 boosters' (Oct 22)
candidates.angle: Myth-correction Short. Show how much berberine, fibre and probiotics actually change GLP-1 levels or weight in trials (modest at best) versus semaglutide trial results. Mention FDA warning letters. Keep it positive: food habits that support your own GLP-1 without replacing the medicine. Name no products.
candidates.why_now: The story is now in its second news wave (Reuters syndicated Oct 23), seen in 3 snapshots, and TikTok-driven.

evidence.signal: Doctors and regulators raise flags as weight-loss drug users turn to supplements.
'The Best GLP-1 Boosters and Supplements (2026)'.

candidates.topic: Semaglutide and alcohol: randomized trial data on heavy drinking (Medical Economics, Oct 23), Heineken's internal worry about GLP-1s and beer sales (Reuters exclusive, Oct 23), and telehealth off-label prescribing for addiction (STAT, Oct 22)
candidates.angle: Benefits-beyond-weight Short. The Heineken hook draws the click, then explain what the RCT showed (adults with alcohol use disorder and obesity, alongside therapy) and that semaglutide is not approved for alcohol use. Encourage talking to a clinician. Never endorse off-label telehealth.
candidates.why_now: Three independent news angles in 48 hours, and the Reuters business hook is mainstream.

evidence.signal: Heineken document reveals worries over weight-loss drugs and beer sales.
Telehealth prescribing GLP-1s off-label for addiction ahead of FDA approval.

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide versus semaglutide for blood pressure: new meta-regression of phase 3 trials (EClinicalMedicine, Oct 12) covered by Verywell Health (Oct 22)
candidates.angle: Indirect head-to-head Short, tirzepatide first. Show how blood pressure falls in step with weight loss across GLP-1 and multi-hormone trials. Name the population (overweight or obesity) and common side effects for each drug. Label it 'across trials, not head-to-head'.
candidates.why_now: Verywell's consumer pickup on Oct 22. Two-drug head-to-heads have a median of 103.

evidence.signal: Weight loss and blood pressure lowering with GLP-1 RAs and multi-hormone modulators: meta-regression of phase 3 trials.
'New Research Shows GLP-1 Drugs May Help Reduce Blood Pressure'.

candidates.topic: Was Zepbound recalled? No. The FDA recall covers compounded 'copycat' tirzepatide vials over sterility concerns (BioPharma Dive Oct 22, The Hill and Dallas News Oct 23–24)
candidates.angle: Gray-market 'what's confirmed?' Short, only if no recall Short has run in the last 7 days. Name the compounder and lots exactly as the FDA lists them, say branded Zepbound and Mounjaro are not part of it, and point to a prescriber or pharmacist.
candidates.why_now: Local TV and newspapers are still running it (Oct 24). We already covered a 'Was Mounjaro recalled?' angle, so this is risky on the variety guard and the one-recall-a-week cap.

evidence.signal: GLP-1 compounder issues recall for copycat Zepbound.
Compounded GLP-1 injections recalled over sterility concerns.

candidates.topic: Can semaglutide affect decision-making in depression? Randomized clinical trial on explore/exploit choices in major depressive disorder (Psychol Med, Oct 21)
candidates.angle: 'Promising early research' Short on GLP-1 and the brain. A small mechanistic RCT, not a depression treatment. Link it to the brain's reward system and 'food noise'. Pull the abstract (it didn't load) before scripting.
candidates.why_now: A fresh RCT with no mainstream coverage. It pairs with the schizophrenia psychiatric-hospitalization coverage (Oct 23) for a brain-health piece.

evidence.signal: Semaglutide modulates explore/exploit decision-making in MDD: an RCT.
GLP-1 drugs linked to fewer psychiatric hospitalizations in schizophrenia with type 2 diabetes.

candidates.topic: REJECT: 'GLP-1 Microdosing: Can a Smaller Dose Still Deliver Results?' (Yahoo Health, Oct 24)
candidates.angle: Do not cover. Microdosing and self-titration protocols are banned by our guardrails. If the question comes up, say only that dosing decisions belong with a prescriber.
candidates.why_now: Mainstream pickup today. Flagged so downstream agents don't use it.

evidence.signal: A microdosing article spreading in mainstream feeds.

candidates.topic: REJECT: 'Retatrutide peptide: quality-control checklist for sourcing research-grade material' (Pharmaceutical Technology, Oct 22) and the needle-free peptide manufacturing PR (TradingView, Oct 22)
candidates.angle: Do not cover. This is sourcing and vendor content for unapproved or research-chemical GLP-1s.
